content.brief: Acme Corp is evaluating a replacement for a manual weekly forecasting process. The CFO owns sign-off and the target go-live is the end of Q1.

sentences.text: Thanks for making the time today, Jane and John.
Honestly, the quarter-end reporting process is broken.
My team rebuilds the pipeline forecast manually in spreadsheets every week and it takes about 20 hours.
What would a good outcome look like?
If forecast prep dropped by 75 percent and forecast error came down to under 10%, it would pay for itself.
I need a single source of truth for pipeline data that syncs with HubSpot automatically.
Understood. Who else weighs in on a decision like this?
I'm the CFO. I sign off on any software spend over $50,000 and I make the final decision on this one.
The money sits in the operations line, roughly $60k per year.
What criteria will you use to compare vendors?
The must-haves are native HubSpot integration, SOC 2 Type II, and role-based permissions.
You can reach the IT lead at it.lead@acme.example or 555-201-3344 for the security questions.
And the path from here to a signed agreement?
After a technical demo it goes through IT security review, then procurement, then legal review of the MSA.
Timing matters too. The board wants this live by the end of Q1 so the new forecast process can launch at the April kickoff.
Next step: I will send over a proposal and schedule a technical demo with your IT lead.
